The run-in to the exam. **All times are given in both Korea (KST) and UK (BST)**; while the UK is on summer
time, **KST = UK + 8 h**. Sessions are twice-plus per week. Homework links go straight to the clinic assignment
for that topic.

::: {.callout-important}
## How to use the back half — review beats volume

The second half is mock-heavy. The point of a mock is **not** the score — it is the **review**. So:

1. **Sit every mock cold** — full time limit, no calculator, no breaks, no peeking.
2. **Mark it, then spend as long on the review as on the paper.** Every wrong or guessed question → name the
   topic → redo it properly → note the "one move" you missed.
3. If time is short, **drop a mock rather than skip a review.** Roughly 11 full papers sit in the back half;
   getting real value from 7 of them beats rushing all 11.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Three tweaks to the plan (worth making)

- **23 Sep is Coordinate geometry, not Parametric.** *Parametric & locus is beyond the TMUA spec (a MAT
  topic).* The question you actually got wrong twice — "normal to a curve" (2016 Q3, 2018 Q11) — is
  **coordinate geometry**, so run the **[Coordinate geometry clinic](../../lessons/coordinate_geometry_clinic/class_material.qmd)** instead.
- **Keep the 2023 paper pristine for 14 Oct.** The plan reviews 2023 P1/P2 as homework on 25 Sep *and* sits
  2023 as the final cold mock on 14 Oct — by then you'll have seen it. For the 25 Sep review, use a paper you
  have **already sat** (e.g. **2018**) so 2023 stays fresh for the real dress rehearsal.
- **Guard your pace in every mock.** Whatever else, keep the "**last 5 questions in 15 minutes**" habit and a
  "flag-and-move after 4 minutes" rule — that is where the marks leak.
:::
